memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And these tribes shall stand on Mount Ebal to pronounce curses: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali." — Deut 27:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Six tribes stood on Mount Ebal, the mountain of the curse. This was the sobering half of the ceremony. God did not only speak of blessing; He also spoke honestly about the consequences of turning from Him. The curse was not God being cruel — it was God being truthful about what happens when His people abandon His ways.

We live in a time that prefers to hear only about blessing and comfort. We would rather skip the hard warnings. But a God who never warned us of danger would not be loving; He would be neglectful. A parent who never warns a child away from fire does not love the child well. God's warnings are an expression of His care.

The reality of the curse also does something else for us — it magnifies the mercy of the gospel. If there were no real curse, we would not grasp how great our rescue is. But because sin genuinely brings a curse (Rom 6:23), the news that Christ bore it for us becomes stunningly good.

So do not resent the "Ebal" passages of Scripture. Let them sober you and drive you to Christ. He faced the full weight of the curse so that all who trust Him need never bear it. The mountain of cursing makes the cross shine all the brighter.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I take God's warnings seriously, or only want to hear comfort?
2. How do the warnings of Scripture actually show God's love?
3. How does the reality of the curse make Christ's rescue more precious?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Your warnings flow from Your love. Help me take them to heart, and lead me always to the cross where Christ bore the curse for me. Amen.
